title: Eight of Swords Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Eight of Swords upright: feeling trapped, self-doubt, limiting beliefs; reversed: breaking free. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Ask your question.
h1: Eight of Swords Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Eight of Swords, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a blindfolded woman in red, bound with gray bands, stands among eight swords, a castle behind.
capsule: The Eight of Swords means feeling trapped: restriction, self-doubt and limiting beliefs that make a situation look more closed than it is. Reversed, the knots loosen and a way out comes into view. It is a hard card with a hopeful core, since the trap is rarely total. The answer is no: the figure is still bound and blindfolded.

blocks.heading: What is on the Eight of Swords card?
paragraphs: Waite draws "a woman, bound and hoodwinked, with the swords of the card about her" (p. 238); hoodwinked means blindfolded. The swords are the largest shape on the card, planted in the ground around her like a fence.

On the 1909 card she wears a long red-orange robe, with a gray band over her eyes and more gray bands wound around her arms and body. Three swords stand to her left and five to her right, and the ground in front of her is open. Puddles of water lie at her feet, a castle sits on a rocky height behind her, and VIII is printed at the top.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Eight of Swords?
paragraphs: Waite's list is blunt, running from bad news and crisis to treachery (p. 238), and Arcana Diary does not read the card as a forecast of trouble.

His own key line comes before the list: it is "rather a card of temporary durance than of irretrievable bondage" (p. 238). The restraint is real, but in Waite's words it is not meant to last, and that is the thread the modern meaning follows.

blocks.heading: What does the Eight of Swords mean upright?
paragraphs: Feeling trapped is the plain meaning: stuck in a job, a relationship, a routine or a decision, with no good exit in sight. The restriction may be real, yet much of it often comes from inside, from self-doubt, fear of getting it wrong, or limiting beliefs that say you cannot or that no other option exists.

The picture makes the point without words. The swords stand on two sides, but nothing blocks the way ahead; the blindfold is what keeps her from seeing it. Overthinking and waiting to be rescued both keep the bands tight.
What would I try if I believed I had more choice than I think?

blocks.heading: What does the Eight of Swords mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the Eight of Swords can show breaking free: fears loosening, the blindfold slipping, a new perspective that reveals more room than you expected. A way out may already be visible; what remains is to take the first step through it.

It can also mean the opposite pull, knowing you could leave yet staying frozen, or tightening the knots with more worry. This reversed reading is modern; Waite's reversed list is a second string of troubles (p. 238).

blocks.heading: What does the Eight of Swords mean in love?
paragraphs: Self-doubt does most of the binding when this card turns up in love: not feeling good enough, not daring to ask for what you need, staying because leaving feels impossible rather than because you choose to stay.

Without a partner, it can describe holding back from someone new because past hurt insists it will go wrong. With one, it asks how much of the stuck feeling is the situation and how much is the story told about it. Reversed, there is courage to speak, to be seen, or to step out of a pattern that kept you small.

blocks.heading: What does the Eight of Swords mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Boxed in by a role, by rules, by the belief that no other job would have you: at work this is the card of feeling stuck. Test that belief with one fact, such as an application, a conversation or a skill you could learn.
Debt, a tight budget or a fixed cost that seems to close every door is how the trap looks with money, along with the sense that nothing can change. Reversed, options start to show.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Eight of Swords?
paragraphs: Find one fact that contradicts a belief that holds you back, and say it out loud. Then take one small step in the open direction, just to feel that the ground is there.

blocks.heading: Is the Eight of Swords a yes or no card?
The Eight of Swords as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: As a person, the Eight of Swords is someone who feels hemmed in and doubts their own options: capable, but held back by fear or overthinking, waiting for permission that never quite arrives. In you, it is the voice that insists there is no exit. As feelings, the card means feeling stuck or powerless: wanting to come closer or to leave, yet held back by fear, guilt or circumstances. Reversed, those feelings free up: courage returns, doubts ease, and there is more readiness to act on what is felt.

blocks.heading: The Eight of Swords with other cards

pairs.text: Two blindfolds: a choice put off and a trap assumed. Take one off and look.
Bonds that feel fixed but sit loosely. Ask what keeps you there.
A moment of clarity cuts through the bands; one clear thought changes the picture.
Quiet courage facing fear. Gentle persistence loosens what force cannot.

blocks.heading: Eight of Swords or Two of Swords?
paragraphs: Waite's Two of Swords also shows "a hoodwinked female figure", but she sits and balances two swords upon her shoulders (p. 250). The Two of Swords is a choice put off, a balance kept by not looking; the Eight is the feeling of being hemmed in. In the Two she holds the swords herself; in the Eight they surround her.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Eight of Swords
paragraphs: Which limit have I actually tested?
What story about myself keeps me where I am?
Who could help me see the open side?

faq.q: Is the Eight of Swords a good or bad card?
faq.a: It is a hard card, but not a hopeless one. It names a stuck feeling honestly and then points to the open ground the blindfold hides. Many people find it a relief: if part of the problem lies in how things are seen, part of the answer does too.

faq.q: Does the Eight of Swords mean I am stuck in my relationship?
faq.a: Not as a fact about your life. In love it traditionally describes feeling stuck: unsure how to move forward, afraid to speak up, or doubting that other choices exist. It asks how much of that is circumstance and how much is fear, and only you can sort that out, perhaps with someone you trust.

faq.q: Does the Eight of Swords mean playing the victim?
faq.a: It can describe a victim mindset: the sense that things are done to you and you have no say. The card does not blame you for it; it shows how that view keeps you still. Taking back even one small choice is how the card turns around.

waite.quote: Bad news, violent chagrin, crisis, censure, power in trammels, conflict, calumny; also sickness. Reversed: Disquiet, difficulty, opposition, accident, treachery; what is unforeseen; fatality.
